action: A dog in a snowy yard walks a few steps to the left with its head forward, then is suddenly seen facing the other way, hunched, and finally walks to the right toward the water bowl.
identity_gap: The doodle's defining construction, a long wedge-shaped head with a large almond eye joined to a boxy rear block with a comb of many wobbly leg strokes, is not carried; the cartoon dog changes construction from frame to frame (thin head-up stick figure, front-facing hunched body, then a clean conventional side-view dog) and never has the doodle's boxy multi-leg rear.
notes: Frames 2-4 hold together as a leftward walk and the frame 2-4 head is the closest echo of the doodle's wedge head, but frame 1 reads as a different, upright animal, frames 5-6 flip direction and switch to a front three-quarter pose, and frames 7-8 are a third, tidier drawing walking right. The stroke weight matches the doodle, but the simplifications and the proportions do not.
